about: measure contests of 2018 in Colorado, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, 2018 precinct-level returns, GitHub MEDSL/2018-elections-official at commit 42055b11dcd5
medsl.licence: no licence file in the repository; MEDSL's Dataverse sets of the same year are CC0 1.0
medsl.note: MEDSL's own earlier release, read by git (the repository now points to its Dataverse sets, which sit behind a guestbook; pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py --compare-dataverse matches the files by MD5); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files 2018-co-precinct-general.zip

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

nara.name: National Archives, Electoral College Results (the sitting president's party)
nara.licence: US federal public record; no licence printed

source.name: Colorado Legislative Council Staff, 2018 State Ballot Information Booklet (Blue Book), English

ballot_text.type_quote: Amendment 73 proposes amending the Colorado Constitution and Colorado statutes to:

fact.quote: Under provisions in the state constitution, passage of a constitutional amendment requires at least 55 percent of the votes cast, except that when a constitutional amendment is limited to a repeal, it requires a simple majority vote. In 2018, Amendments V, W, X, Y, and Z, and Amendments 73, 74, and 75 require 55 percent of the vote to pass, and Amendment A requires a simple majority vote.
fact.why: Initiated measure that adds new constitutional subsection art. IX sec. 17(4.5) and also changes statutes (adds text). Type is a constitutional amendment (it also amends C.R.S.; Blue Book counts it as the one measure changing both). Blue Book lists 73 among the amendments that 'require 55 percent'. The Blue Book itself applies the repeal-only rule and prints the threshold for this measure, so applies is read directly from the Legislative Council's own statement (one logical step: 55 percent means not limited to a repeal).

source.name: Colorado Legislative Council Staff, 2018 State Ballot Information Booklet (Blue Book), English
